summary: Industrial experience report (Uber; ASE-Industry 2026) on DragonCrawl V2, a GPT-4o mobile end-to-end regression gate. Test owners write a natural-language intent, steps and mid-state assertions. The model picks each next UI action from a canonicalised view hierarchy and judges end states from screenshots, and backend tool calls set up states such as driver-document approval. The paper reports 91.6% iOS / 92.2% Android pass rates over 1,013 production flows, per-flow authoring time of 2.5h median vs about 4 days for the embedding-based V1, a component ablation (5 runs x 1,013 flows), and an estimated 27 developer-years saved.

claims.claim: V2 reaches 91.6% (iOS) / 92.2% (Android) pass rate vs 80-82% for V1.
claims.evidence: Table 2. V1 was measured on about 48 low-complexity flows in 2023 and V2 on 1,013 flows aggregated over months of CI, so the populations differ. A 'pass' means the agent reached the end state; the false-pass rate (real defects the gate missed) is never measured. VQA accuracy is asserted 'near-perfect' by citing the authors' prior work.

claims.claim: Test onboarding drops from 96-120 hours to under 4 hours.
claims.evidence: Table 6 reports V1 as 4 days median (5 days p75/p90) and V2 as 2.5h median (4h p90). The abstract's '96-120 hours' converts days at 24 h/day while V2 is in working hours, which inflates the ratio. At an 8-hour working day V1 is 32-40 h, a reduction of about 13x, not 30-40x. The V1 sample is 'small and limited to low-complexity flows'.

claims.claim: Prompt constraints and view-hierarchy canonicalisation each contribute.
claims.evidence: Table 5: 5,065 executions per configuration (5 runs x 1,013 flows) on a frozen app build: full 95.9% success, without prompt constraints 89.6%, without canonicalisation 91.7%, with action counts and time also reported. Variance across the five runs is not reported, but n is large. This is the only controlled result.

claims.claim: About 27 developer-years saved; feature velocity +15%; bug escape rate decreased.
claims.evidence: §6.4: a counterfactual with assumed constants (16 h authoring plus 20 h maintenance per manual test, 1,380 h/year) times 1,013 tests, not measured effort. The +15% velocity and the lower bug-escape rate (§6.5) come with no method or data. The bug-resolution median of 30.4 h vs 'approximately 5 days' has an unsourced baseline and is confounded by auto-filing tickets to the PR owner.

patterns.note: Tests are authored as a natural-language intent plus steps plus explicit mid-state and end-state assertions with priorities. The V1 -> V2 comparison changes model, history and assertions at once, so the structured-criteria format itself is not isolated.
A GPT-4o screenshot judge decides end-state and mid-state assertions and blocks commits. No false-pass or false-fail rates are reported here; validity is asserted from the authors' prior work.

Deterministic canonicalisation of the raw view hierarchy (e.g. 144 nodes -> 51 actions) vs the raw hierarchy: 95.9% vs 91.7% success, fewer actions, less time, over 5,065 executions per arm. This is structural filtering, not LLM summarisation; Uber apps and one model only.
A real production deployment, but all impact numbers are uncontrolled before/after comparisons or counterfactual estimates.
SDETs repositioned as 'context engineers' who curate personas, environment parameters, tool-call templates and MCPs for the agent. Anecdotal; not measured.
Daily divergence detection against a 10,000-trajectory golden set, with weekly deduplicated human triage (about 5% of reviewer time). Not evaluated against an alternative.
Reports a learning curve (intent definitions too vague or too specific) and SDET upskilling in prompt engineering. Anecdotal; no comprehension measure.

methodology.sample: 1,013 production flows on two Uber apps (iOS, Android); ablation 5,065 executions per configuration; 98 high-priority bugs for resolution time.
methodology.baselines: Own V1 (embedding plus K-D tree) on a different, smaller flow set; external tools' self-reported completion rates (Table 3), which the authors call not like-for-like.
methodology.variance: None reported; ablation uses 5 runs per flow, but the spread is not given.
methodology.ablations: Prompt constraints and view canonicalisation; backend tool calling argued to be non-ablatable (23.1% of flows depend on it).
methodology.languages: Mobile apps (iOS, Android); implementation languages not stated; Python test-definition tooling.

standards.artifacts: None: code, prompts, models and data are proprietary to Uber.

biases.detail: Developer-years saved, velocity +15% and maintenance overhead 30-40% -> 5% are internal estimates with no stated method.
Pass rate measures that the agent completes the flow, not that the gate catches regressions; the miss rate for real defects is never reported.
Compared only with its own deprecated V1 on a different flow population; no scripted Appium/Espresso suite or current LLM-agent baseline on the same flows.
'Paradigm shift from pattern matching to genuine understanding', and the onboarding hours inflated by a days-to-hours conversion.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Uber's internal DragonCrawl (not sold); OpenAI GPT-4o as a component
coi.detail: Company engineers evaluate their own internal system with no independent check. It is not a commercial product, so the incentive is reputational rather than sales.

verdict_reason: A real, large-scale industrial deployment with one solid controlled ablation. The headline numbers are uncontrolled before/after comparisons, counterfactual estimates or unit-inflated: '96-120 hours' converts days at 24 h/day, and the 27 developer-years is assumption-driven. The gate's false-pass rate is never measured.
applicability: Only marginal for discovery and onboarding: 'onboarding' here means authoring a new test flow, not onboarding developers. Two things transfer to the Java team's spec-driven work. (1) Writing acceptance as a natural-language intent plus explicit prioritised mid-state and end-state assertions, with tool calls to set backend state, is a workable format for API-level acceptance checks of ingestion flows. Pair it with a measured false-pass rate, which this paper lacks. (2) Deterministically trimming large structured context (here a view hierarchy) to the actionable elements before the model sees it measurably helped; the analogue is pre-filtering schemas or service graphs before handing them to an exploration agent.
